## Overview

The Nenets are a Samoyedic ethnic group native to the Russian Arctic and the Russian Far North. They live mainly in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, Nenets Autonomous Okrug and Taymyrsky Dolgano-Nenetsky District, along the coastline of the Arctic Ocean near the Arctic Circle between the Kola and Taymyr peninsulas. Other settlement areas include the basin of the Pur and Taz rivers and the east of the Khanty-Mansiysk Autonomous Okrug – Yugra. According to the 2021 census, there were 49,787 Nenets in Russia. They are divided into Tundra Nenets and Forest Nenets, whose languages belong to the Samoyedic branch of the Uralic language family. Their folk culture is closely associated with reindeer herding, fishing, migration, conical housing, sacred objects and oral performance.

## Material culture

### Textile & pattern traditions

**Motif vocabulary.** The supplied sources name no Nenets textile motifs.

### Clothing & dress

The sources mention *parka*, a traditional long, hooded jacket made from skins and sometimes fur. During migrations, Nenets people carried sacred items including bear skins, religious figures and coins on a holy sleigh.

### Architecture

Nenets housing is described as a conical yurt called *mya*.

### Ceramics, metalwork & everyday objects

They mention coins and religious figures among the objects placed on the sacred sleigh, and describe the reindeer sled as part of migration and religious practice.

### Jewelry & body adornment

Coins are mentioned as objects placed on the sacred sleigh, but not as personal adornment.

## Music & performance

Traditional Nenets music includes epic poems comparable to the Finnish Kalevala and the Yakut Olonkho. The sources state that traditional Nenets music uses neither musical instruments nor dance.

The sources describe the Nenets as having a shamanistic and animistic belief system. The Nenets shaman is called a *Tadibya*. Sacred objects, including bear skins, religious figures and coins, were placed on a holy sleigh during migrations. The contents were unpacked only during special occasions or religious rituals such as sacrifices, and only esteemed elders were allowed to unpack them.

The Nenets language article states that Tundra Nenets has a literary tradition going back to the 1930s, while Forest Nenets was first written during the 1990s and has been little documented.

## Dance & theatre

Traditional Nenets music is described as using neither musical instruments nor dance.

## Festivals & rituals

They do describe religious rituals within the context of migration. Nenets people placed sacred items such as bear skins, religious figures and coins on a holy sleigh. These objects were unpacked only during special occasions or religious rituals, including sacrifices, and only esteemed elders were permitted to unpack the sacred sleigh.

Nenets belief is described as shamanistic and animistic, with an emphasis on respect for the land and its resources. Nenets people also designate sacred spots where they make requests of the spirits for a successful migration. The sources state that these sacred spots can be marked by wooden pegs. No further information is supplied about birth, coming-of-age, wedding or funeral rites.

The sources also describe the effects of Soviet collectivization after the Russian Revolution. The government attempted to make nomadic Samoyeds settle permanently, and children were educated in state boarding schools. These policies contributed to the erosion of cultural identity, while many Nenets later worked to preserve their traditional nomadic lifestyle.

## Foodways

The sources identify reindeer meat and fish as important components of Nenets foodways. Their main subsistence comes from hunting and reindeer herding, while fish is a major part of the diet. Fishing is especially important in summer. Industrial development has degraded freshwater sources, reduced fish populations and occupied fishing grounds used by Nenets people. Reindeer herding is central to the economy and way of life of many Nenets families, and reindeer are also used as draft animals throughout the year, allowing people to cover great distances.

## Oral tradition & literature

Traditional Nenets music includes epic poems comparable to the Finnish Kalevala and the Yakut Olonkho.

Since the 1930s, some Nenets have expressed themselves professionally through cultural media. Tyko Vylka and Konstantin Pankov became well-known painters. Anna Nerkagi is identified as one of the most celebrated Nenets writers, while Yuri Vella became the first writer in the Forest Nenets language. Yuri Vella is also described as a reindeer herder, writer, poet, environmentalist and social activist.

The language sources state that Tundra Nenets has a literary tradition dating to the 1930s. Forest Nenets was first written during the 1990s and remains little documented. The sources also mention the Red Book on endangered languages, Nenets language-learning materials and a Forest Nenets–English glossary.

## Language & religion

Nenets languages are classified in the Samoyedic branch of the Uralic language family. The two closely related languages are Tundra Nenets and Forest Nenets, which are often treated as dialects but have low mutual intelligibility. Tundra Nenets has the higher number of speakers and is spoken from the Kanin Peninsula to the Yenisei River. Forest Nenets is spoken around the Agan, Pur, Lyamin and Nadym rivers. Both languages have been influenced by Russian; Tundra Nenets has also been influenced by Komi and Northern Khanty, while Forest Nenets has been influenced by Eastern Khanty.

The sources describe Nenets religion as shamanistic and animistic, emphasizing respect for land and resources. The shaman is called a *Tadibya*. UNESCO classifies Nenets as an endangered language. The sources also state that many Nenets, especially in the Nenets Autonomous Okrug, lost their mother tongue and became assimilated.

## Sources & further reading

- *Samoyedes*, *Encyclopædia Britannica*, vol. 24, 11th ed., 1911.
- [Nenets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nenets)
- [Nenets language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nenets_language)
- [Nenets music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nenets_music)
